edges.description: Loss of the transporter reduces melanosome number in a pigmented epithelium in vivo, supporting the requirement for ABCB6 in melanosome maturation.
edges.limitations: The readout is melanosome number in the retinal pigment epithelium, not in skin melanocytes, and a knockout models absence of the transporter whereas the human disease is caused by heterozygous missense alleles that are mislocalised rather than absent. The translational gap is wider than an absent skin readout: complete knockout of Abcb6 in a pigmented C57BL/6 strain produced no detectable abnormality of pigmentation, eye morphology or balance, so the mouse does not reproduce the human phenotype at the organism level at all.

edges.description: Knockdown reduces mature melanocyte number, supporting a requirement for the transporter in melanocyte maturation.
edges.limitations: A morpholino knockdown models absence of the transporter, whereas the human disease is caused by heterozygous missense alleles that are mislocalised rather than absent. The readout is mature melanocyte number, not melanosome maturation, and the model does not reproduce the mottled pattern that defines the human disease.

evidence.reference_title: Genome-wide linkage, exome sequencing and functional analyses identify ABCB6 as the pathogenic gene of dyschromatosis universalis hereditaria.
evidence.snippet: Genome-wide linkage (assuming autosomal dominant inheritance mode) and exome sequencing analyses identified ABCB6 as the disease candidate gene by discovering a coding mutation (c.1358C>T; p.Ala453Val) that co-segregates with the disease phenotype.

nodes.description: A constitutive Abcb6 knockout mouse. Morphological analysis of its retinal pigment epithelium shows significantly fewer melanosomes, which is the in vivo counterpart of the melanosome maturation block that the siRNA and rescue experiments establish in cells.

ABCB6 is required for the early steps of melanogenesis that build the PMEL amyloid matrix on which melanin is deposited. Without it, PMEL amyloidogenesis is impaired and pigmented melanosomes accumulate aberrant multilamellar material.

nodes.description: Wild-type ABCB6 sits in an endosome-like compartment and at melanocyte dendrite tips. Disease variants are retained in the Golgi instead, so the transporter never reaches the membrane where it acts.

evidence.reference_title: Mutations in ABCB6 cause dyschromatosis universalis hereditaria.
evidence.snippet: Examination of subcellular localization of wild-type ABCB6 in a B16 mouse melanoma cell line revealed that it is localized to the endosome-like compartment and dendrite tips, whereas disease-causing mutations of ABCB6 resulted in its retention in the Golgi apparatus.

nodes.description: The defining skin finding: irregular hyperpigmented macules interspersed with hypopigmented ones over trunk and limbs. The face is involved in about half of patients.

evidence.reference_title: Dyschromatosis universalis hereditaria.
evidence.snippet: DUH is characterized by multiple irregular hyperpigmented macules interspersed with hypopigmented macules in a mottled pattern over the trunk and extremities. The face is involved in 50% of individuals.

nodes.description: The maturation block does not fall equally on every melanocyte, which is what makes the skin mottled rather than uniformly pale. Melanocytes under hyperpigmented skin hold more mature melanized melanosomes; those under hypopigmented skin hold empty immature ones.

evidence.reference_title: Novel mutations of ABCB6 associated with autosomal dominant dyschromatosis universalis hereditaria.
evidence.snippet: Histopathological analysis showed melanocytes in normal control's skin tissue and the hyperpigmented area contained more melanized, mature melanosomes than those within the hypopigmented areas. Empty immature melanosomes were found in the hypopigmented melanocytes.

nodes.description: The one reported frameshift allele, found in an unrelated sporadic patient and absent from 455 ethnically matched controls. Written g.776delC at the genomic level by the source.

nodes.description: Missense variant c.1358C>T in exon 7, cosegregating in one Chinese family and confirmed in further families by Sanger sequencing.

evidence.reference_title: A novel mutation in ABCB6 associated with dyschromatosis universalis hereditaria in a Saudi family.
evidence.snippet: Here we describe 2 new cases of DUH in a Saudi mother and her son associated with a novel mutation (c.1144G>A; p.G382R) in the ABCB6 gene.

nodes.description: Missense variant c.1736G>A in exon 12. In a melanocytic cell line it fails to restore PMEL fibril formation, so it is the DUH allele with a direct functional readout.

evidence.reference_title: ABCB6 Resides in Melanosomes and Regulates Early Steps of Melanogenesis Required for PMEL Amyloid Matrix Formation.
evidence.snippet: PMEL fibril formation and normal maturation of pigmented melanosomes could be restored by the overexpression of wild-type ABCB6 but not by variants containing an inactivating catalytic mutation (K629M) or the G579E DUH mutation.

nodes.description: Missense variant c.1067T>C in exon 3, found in a five-generation Chinese DUH family.

nodes.description: Missense variant c.508A>G in exon 1, found by mutational screening of sporadic DUH patients rather than in a pedigree, so it carries no cosegregation evidence.

evidence.reference_title: Mutations in ABCB6 cause dyschromatosis universalis hereditaria.
evidence.snippet: Two additional missense mutations, c.508A>G (p.Ser170Gly) in exon 1 and c.1736G>A (p.Gly579Glu) in exon 12 of ABCB6, were found in two out of six patients by mutational screening using sporadic DUH patients.

nodes.description: Missense variant c.964A>C in exon 4, discovered in a second family where it was heterozygous in all seven affected and absent in all seven unaffected members. First reported as p.Ser322Lys, which is the name the discovering paper uses and which a later group corrected to p.Ser322Arg. The cDNA change confirms the correction: c.964A>C changes the first base of codon 322 from AGC to CGC, serine to arginine, and no single A>C substitution at that position can give lysine. The same paper's own Figure 2C legend writes p.S322L, so it is not internally consistent on this allele either.

evidence.reference_title: Genome-wide linkage, exome sequencing and functional analyses identify ABCB6 as the pathogenic gene of dyschromatosis universalis hereditaria.
evidence.snippet: Further mutation analysis of ABCB6 in four other DUH families and two sporadic cases by Sanger sequencing confirmed the mutation (c.1358C>T; p.Ala453Val) and discovered a second, co-segregating coding mutation (c.964A>C; p.Ser322Lys) in one of the four families.

nodes.description: Morpholinos against exons 6 and 8 of the zebrafish ABCB6 homolog, which correspond to exons 4 and 7 of human ABCB6. Knockdown reduces the number of mature melanocytes in the head region at 5 dpf, and co-injecting full-length human ABCB6 mRNA partially rescues that phenotype. No gene identifier is recorded because zebrafish has two ABCB6 paralogs and the paper does not say which one its morpholinos target; see the entry notes for the searches behind that statement.
